correctness.rationale: The support-line formula gives L_j(r)=kappa(1-r_j)/(1-r_j+c r_j), since the supports of the two summands add to one. At c=1 the shifted supports would lie in a cyclic eigenspace with eigenvalue strictly between the k=1 and k=2 values, so the shift vanishes. At c≠1 write D=1-r+c r and c=(1-lambda)^2/lambda^2: the transformed x is lambda D/(1-lambda), and lambda^2 D+(1-2lambda)(1-r)=(1-lambda)^2 verifies the reciprocal substitution with positive x. In the recurrence proof the reciprocal first moment makes adjacent characters orthonormal in the 1/x-weighted inner product. The multiplier identity follows from -mu_k=4 sin((k-1)alpha) sin((k+1)alpha) and cotangent subtraction; the cotangent differences telescope to 2 cot(alpha). Equality in the resulting Bessel sum would force both s_2=s_4=1, impossible for distinct characters on a grid with strictly positive weights. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz is therefore strict for nonzero higher-mode part h. Expanding the weighted square of x minus its constant and first-harmonic parts then gives B(x)≤kappa N, with equality only if both parts beyond the constant vanish. The recurrence imposes equality and x=1. At N=4 opposite equations give x_0=x_2, x_1=x_3 and x_0 x_1=1. For polygons, opposite sides of each rectangle have equal length; comparing opposite proportionality equations forces equal opposite supports, and the atom formula and converse follow. The frozen NumPy script was inspected, not executed; recorded samples cannot prove strictness at every positive weight, which follows analytically.

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural exceptional case at the even-parity boundary of the weighted Fourier argument. It proves a global discrete uniqueness result in positive supports without assuming central symmetry of the unknown, and identifies exactly where a fixed regular sum can have nonhomothetic proportional-cone-volume summands in the even regular case. The square family explains why the boundary cannot simply be removed.
